question: Should OpenClaw adopt Gmail Pub/Sub pull delivery as the staged first-party direction, while preserving the existing push path until opt-in implementation and dogfood evidence support any later default change?
rationale: The RFC intentionally introduces future product, configuration, and compatibility surface across gog, OpenClaw, and downstream packaging; source alignment cannot determine whether that long-term direction should be accepted.

options.title: Accept the staged pull direction
options.body: Accept the RFC as the design contract, require opt-in implementation and preserved push compatibility first, and defer any default flip to a later proof-backed PR.

options.title: Request a narrower RFC
options.body: Keep the pull-consumer design but remove or defer downstream packaging and default-path commitments until the first implementation is proven.

options.title: Reject the direction
options.body: Retain the current push-oriented Gmail watch model and close this RFC without treating its linked implementation drafts as accepted direction.

recommendation.title: Accept the staged pull direction
recommendation.body: Accept the RFC as the design contract, require opt-in implementation and preserved push compatibility first, and defer any default flip to a later proof-backed PR.

likelyOwner.reason: joshp123 is the best available proposal-context owner from branch history and discussion, although RFC acceptance itself requires an authorized repository decision-maker.
